purpose: Translates user-authored pipeline Python (the `@pipeline.<type>` decorator DSL) into the canonical `PipelineGraph` model the GUI/executor/codegen consume, and is the inverse of codegen for the parse->edit->save round-trip. Two parse paths: (1) the healthy `ast`-based path that walks top-level FunctionDefs, resolves node configs (inline kwargs or JSON sidecars), derives edges (explicit `pipeline.connect` calls, implicit param-name matching, or linear-order fallback), and recursively parses/merges `pipeline.submodel("path")` references into hierarchical or flattened graphs; (2) a regex-anchored fallback for files that fail `ast.parse`, which locates decorator/connect/meta sites textually but re-parses recovered fragments with the real AST so values keep fidelity, failing loud when a visible fragment cannot be recovered. A separate sub-region (`_expression_parser.py`) is a Polars-expression-to-human-text/evaluator used by the trace subsystem, NOT by the graph parser.

internal_dataflow: parse_pipeline_file reads text via read_user_text (utf-8, errors=replace), infers project root for sidecar/submodel resolution, then parse_pipeline_source: ast.parse(source) -> on SyntaxError delegate to _parser_regex.fallback_parse; else _extract_pipeline_meta (name/desc), _extract_function_bodies (raw body source keyed by func name), _extract_decorated_nodes (walk top-level FunctionDefs whose decorator matches _is_pipeline_node_decorator -> _get_decorator_kwargs via _eval_ast_literal -> _resolve_node_config: load JSON sidecar OR _build_node_config from kwargs, extract user code from body via _code_extraction matcher/finaliser registry, validate user-declared Contract). Edges: _extract_connect_calls (module-level pipeline.connect chains) + implicit param-name matching + linear-order fallback (_build_edges). _build_rf_nodes -> GraphNode list. preamble/preserved_blocks extracted textually. Submodels: extract_submodel_calls -> resolve_submodel_reference (sandbox-checked) -> parse_submodel_file (recursive) -> merge_submodels (build submodel__<name> placeholder, classify_ports, rewire_edges to in__/out__ handles; if flatten -> flatten_graph dissolves placeholders). Finally validate_pipeline_graph_shape_contracts enforces Explore in/out-degree. _expression_parser is a separate flow: code string -> ast.parse -> _ExprConverter walks the with_columns expr AST to text + referenced cols/constants; _ExprEvaluator/_BranchTrackingEvaluator re-walk to compute a single-row value and taken/dimmed branches.
concurrency_model: Stateless, synchronous, single-threaded pure functions; no shared mutable module state in the parse path (compiled regexes and registry dicts are read-only). Parsing is invoked during `haute serve` startup and on every GUI load; the docstring on _derive_parse_time_contract notes parse-time must NOT block on remote I/O (MODEL_SCORE contract derivation is deliberately kept local to avoid blocking the server before it binds its port). _io._load_cached uses functools.lru_cache (external object loading) but that is runtime, not parse. No locks; re-entrancy via recursive submodel parsing is bounded only by filesystem structure (see cycle risk).
perf_characteristics: Dominated by ast.parse (one parse of the whole module on the healthy path; the fallback and several helpers re-parse fragments). Multiple full-source textual scans per parse: _extract_preamble, _extract_preserved_blocks, and the regex fallback's _iter_connect_anchor_matches / _position_is_code / _parenthesized_wrapper_depth_before each rescan from index 0, giving the fallback path roughly O(n^2) character work for large broken files (each connect/decorator anchor triggers a from-zero string-literal scan to classify its position). _expression_parser re-parses the same code up to ~5 times per target column (parse_expression, _compute_result, _evaluate_conditional_branches, and again per column in parse_expression_chain) and uses ast.walk repeatedly; fine for node-sized snippets, not for large bodies. Submodel parsing is recursive and re-reads/re-parses each referenced file.
invariants: Round-trip safety: parse(codegen(graph)) must be structurally equivalent to graph, and codegen(parse(file)) must preserve pricing semantics. Extracted user code is always emitted in STATEMENT form (df = ...) never a bare expression, so re-emitting through codegen is a fixpoint (_unwrap_chain_assignment / _strip_redundant_rhs_wrapper_once prove paren removal via AST identity).

Decorator/connect/meta kwargs must be literal Python values (or the sanctioned Contract(...) constructor). Non-literal expressions fail loud via ParseError on BOTH the healthy and fallback paths — returning source text would silently rewrite e.g. cols=COLS into the string 'COLS' on the next save (_eval_ast_literal, _get_decorator_kwargs, _parse_decorator_kwargs_regex).

Fallback recovery is loud-or-faithful: a connect()/decorator/meta fragment that is VISIBLE but unrecoverable (unclosed paren, unparseable span, trailing text) raises ParseError rather than dropping the edge/node — a plausible-but-incomplete graph would corrupt the file on save. Commented-out / in-string occurrences contribute nothing (must match the healthy AST parser).

Node type is determined by the explicit type-specific decorator (@pipeline.<type>), mapped through DECORATOR_TO_NODE_TYPE; config-folder node types MUST reference a JSON sidecar (has_config_folder) or ConfigError is raised.

Submodel path resolution never escapes the resolved project root: resolve_submodel_reference raises ValueError if a candidate is not is_relative_to(project_root); config_path_for_node / load_node_config enforce the same for sidecars.

Edge derivation precedence: explicit pipeline.connect edges, then implicit param-name==node-name edges (skipping pairs already explicit and self-loops), then — only if zero edges and >1 node — a linear chain in definition order.

connect() is chainable (returns Self): every .connect link in a module-level chain whose base receiver is the bare Name 'pipeline'/'submodel' contributes an edge in source order; module.pipeline.connect / get_pipeline().connect are rejected.

Submodel boundary edges use in__<child> / out__<child> handles in hierarchical form; flatten_graph must rewire them back to direct child edges and dedupe, leaving no edge referencing a submodel__ node.
Explore nodes must have exactly one incoming edge and zero outgoing edges (validate_graph_shape_contracts), enforced on the parent graph and each collapsed submodel child graph.

_extract_function_bodies requires the caller to pass the SAME pre-parsed tree used elsewhere (mandatory tree= arg) so source and AST come from one snapshot — prevents a class of silent drift / double-parse masking errors.

User-code extraction must strip only codegen-generated boilerplate and only OUTER-scope returns/aliases: returns inside nested def/class/lambda are preserved (_outermost_returns AST walk, not line heuristics).

candidate_risks.concern: Duplicate top-level function names (two @pipeline.<type> defs with the same name) silently collapse: _extract_function_bodies keys bodies by func name (later def overwrites earlier body), _extract_decorated_nodes emits two raw nodes with identical func_name, and _build_rf_nodes uses func_name as the GraphNode.id — producing two nodes with the same id. Edges/ports/sidecars all key on that id.
candidate_risks.why: Two nodes sharing an id is an undefined state for the GUI, executor, and codegen; the wrong body may be attached to one node, and a save could drop or merge a node — a silent-correctness pricing bug. No de-dup or loud error is present in the parse path.

candidate_risks.concern: Async pipeline node functions are invisible to the healthy parser. _extract_function_bodies and _extract_decorated_nodes only match ast.FunctionDef, never ast.AsyncFunctionDef. A user who writes `@pipeline.polars` over `async def node(...)` gets a node silently dropped from the graph (or only recovered via the regex fallback if the file also has a syntax error).
candidate_risks.why: Silent node loss on save would delete pricing logic; low because async pipeline nodes are likely rare/unsupported, but the failure is silent rather than loud which violates the project's fail-loud principle.

candidate_risks.concern: Recursive submodel parsing (parse_pipeline_source -> parse_submodel_file -> parse_submodel_source) has no cycle detection or depth bound. A submodel that (directly or transitively) references a file that references back would recurse until RecursionError / stack overflow. Note submodels themselves use _is_submodel_node_decorator and extract_submodel_calls only runs in parse_pipeline_source, so a self-referential chain depends on how nested graphs reference each other — worth verifying.
candidate_risks.why: An unbounded recursion on user-controlled file references is a DoS / crash vector during GUI load and `haute lint`.

candidate_risks.concern: _ExprEvaluator silently diverges from real Polars semantics in several places: any None operand short-circuits binops/compares to None/False (Polars null propagation differs for comparisons and boolean ops); .clip parses positional args as (lower, upper) but Polars clip is keyword/positional-sensitive and bound-naming differs across versions; horizontal funcs filter None before min/max/sum (Polars skips nulls but mean_horizontal divides by non-null count which may not match); _eval_horizontal omits all_horizontal/any_horizontal/concat_str entirely (returns None).
candidate_risks.why: These values feed the trace/quote-explanation UI (trace.py, _trace_enrichment.py). A wrong computed value or wrong 'taken branch' is a silent-correctness defect that misleads users debugging prices, even though it does not affect the executor's real output.

candidate_risks.concern: parse_expression and evaluate_expression wrap their whole impl in `except Exception: return opaque/get(target)`. This is a broad catch-all that converts any internal bug (including AttributeError/TypeError from a malformed AST shape) into a silently 'opaque' expression or a fall-through to row_values[target], hiding defects. Contrast with the parser's deliberate fail-loud policy elsewhere.
candidate_risks.why: Silently swallowing all exceptions means real bugs in the converter/evaluator never surface in tests or logs; the UI just shows 'opaque'. Hard-to-notice correctness erosion over time.

candidate_risks.concern: The regex fallback's statement-anchor / wrapper-depth classifiers (_is_top_level_statement_anchor, _parenthesized_wrapper_depth_before, _skip_string_literal) hand-implement Python lexing on deliberately-broken source without tokenize. Edge cases — nested f-strings with quotes/braces, implicit string concatenation, byte strings, line-continuation inside strings, decorators with nested calls spanning many lines — could mis-classify a real connect()/decorator as in-string (dropping it) or vice-versa.
candidate_risks.why: A mis-classified connect() that is dropped (treated as in-string) silently loses an edge on the fallback path without the loud ParseError the design intends; the inverse re-includes commented/string text as an edge. Both are silent graph corruption, only on already-broken files.

candidate_risks.concern: On the HEALTHY path a missing/invalid JSON sidecar raises ConfigError (fail-loud), but on the FALLBACK path a node whose config= cannot be recovered (find_config_by_func_name returns None) for a has_config_folder type raises ConfigError too — meaning ONE syntax error elsewhere in the file plus a config-folder node with an unrecoverable sidecar turns a best-effort recovery into a hard failure, defeating the fallback's purpose of returning a partial graph for the GUI.
candidate_risks.why: Inconsistent failure mode: the fallback is documented to return valid nodes alongside broken ones, but a config-folder node can abort the whole fallback parse. Could surface as the GUI showing nothing instead of error-marked nodes.

candidate_risks.concern: Implicit param-name edges (_build_edges) and reconstructed cross-boundary submodel edges carry no source/target port handles, while explicit connect edges and rewired submodel edges do. The merge logic in merge_submodels reconstructs cross-boundary edges from parent_edges tuples but implicit (param-matched) cross-boundary edges never appear in parent_edges (which comes only from explicit connects), so an implicit edge from a main node into a submodel child may be silently absent from the merged/flattened graph.
candidate_risks.why: A dropped main->submodel-child edge changes the executed DAG (a node loses an input) — a silent pricing-correctness defect specific to the submodel + implicit-edge combination.
candidate_risks.location: src/haute/_parser_submodels.py:135-168 (cross-boundary reconstruction uses explicit parent_edges only); src/haute/_graph_builders.py:142-154 (implicit edges)

candidate_risks.concern: _extract_preamble and _extract_preserved_blocks are purely line/string based (not AST). _extract_preamble keys off the literal stripped lines 'import polars as pl' / 'import haute' and the first 'pipeline =' or '@pipeline.<known type>' line; aliasing imports, multi-line Pipeline() construction, or a decorator line inside a string could mis-bound the preamble, and unmatched preserve-start markers are silently ignored. Preamble round-trips into codegen verbatim.
candidate_risks.why: Mis-captured preamble means user helper code/imports are dropped or duplicated on save (round-trip corruption), and silently-ignored preserve markers lose user-protected code.

candidate_risks.concern: When two submodel references resolve to graphs with the same pipeline_name, parse_pipeline_source only logs a warning ('submodel_name_collision') and overwrites the earlier entry in submodel_graphs/submodel_files. The second submodel silently replaces the first in the merged graph.
candidate_risks.why: Silent loss of an entire submodel subgraph (and its nodes/edges) — a structural pricing-graph defect surfaced only as a log line.

complexity_hotspots.what: _ExprConverter: AST-of-Polars-expression -> human text, with precedence-aware paren insertion, when/then/otherwise chain collection, namespace accessors, horizontal funcs, nested-conditional sub-expression extraction. Highest branching density in the region.

_ExprEvaluator + _BranchTrackingEvaluator: per-method Polars semantics emulation for single-row evaluation and taken/dimmed/nested branch tracking — large method-name dispatch with subtle null/semantic edge cases.

Hand-rolled, string-aware lexing for the broken-file fallback (string-literal skipping, paren-wrapper depth, top-level-statement anchoring, balanced connect-call scanning with chain welding). Dense, security/correctness-sensitive.

Outer-return AST rewriting, provable paren-unwrap by AST identity, and the per-kind boilerplate-matcher + finaliser registry (polars/source/scenario_expander/model_score/rating_step/external) that governs what counts as user code vs codegen scaffold — the core of round-trip fidelity.

region: Code generation (graph/config -> generated pipeline Python) + core graph model
purpose: Converts the React-Flow-style node graph (PipelineGraph/GraphNode + sidecar JSON configs + submodel metadata) into valid, round-trippable haute pipeline `.py` source files (main + `modules/<name>.py`). The generated code must preserve the intended pricing semantics for every node type (sources, transforms, banding, rating steps, model scoring, optimiser apply, scenario expansion, edge joins, submodels) so that a standalone `pipeline.run()` of the saved file behaves identically to the in-canvas executor. This is the SAVE side of a save/parse fixpoint: codegen emits decorated functions + `config=`/`contract=` kwargs + `connect()` calls; the parser (`_config_builder`/`_graph_builders`) must reconstruct the same graph. Semantic fidelity is enforced by sharing the runtime application helpers (`apply_banding_from_config`, `apply_rating_step_from_config`, `score_from_config`, `execute_edge_join`, `load_v2_api_source`) between the generated body and the executor builder, and by a unified `NODE_REGISTRY` so exec and codegen dispatch cannot disagree.

Flow: (1) validate_pipeline_graph_shape_contracts (explore in/out arity) + _error_on_name_collisions across root+all submodel labels (hard error: distinct labels sanitizing to same func name => silent shadowing on import). (2) No-submodel path: _order_edge_join_incoming_edges reorders each edgeJoin's 2 incoming edges into [base, join] role order; _topo_sort orders nodes; _build_id_to_func maps id->_sanitize_func_name(label); _build_node_sources/_build_node_source_ids map target->source func-names/ids in edge order; connect_pairs = (src_func, tgt_func, sourceHandle|None, targetHandle|None). (3) _generate_pipeline_lines emits header (haute.Pipeline/Submodel literal with _safe_str name + description repr), preserved blocks, originals then instances, submodel imports, then connect() calls. (4) Per node, _node_to_code: _role_order_node_sources (edgeJoin reorder) -> _generate_node_code dispatches via NODE_REGISTRY[nodeType].codegen -> for optimiserApply rewrites single passthrough return to the configured ratebook input param -> if has_config_folder, rewrites decorator to `config="config/<folder>/<func>.json"` -> _format_contract_kwarg computes/declares contract and _inject_contract_kwarg splices `contract=...` into the first @pipeline.*/@submodel.* call using a tokenize-based matching-paren scan (string/comment-safe). (5) _assert_emitted_files_parse ast.parse's every emitted file (refuses to write corrupt .py). Submodel path additionally: splits root vs child nodes, emits each submodel to modules/<name>.py with @submodel.* decorators, resolves cross-boundary `in__<child_id>`/`out__<child_id>` handles back to child func names, and maps boundary edges into edge-join target roles via build_edge_join_boundary_target_roles. The generated bodies call shared runtime helpers (apply_banding_from_config, apply_rating_step_from_config, score_from_config, pipeline._apply_edge_join, load_v2_api_source) so standalone run == canvas run. Config sidecars are produced separately by _config_io.collect_node_configs and persisted by SavePipelineService.
concurrency_model: Codegen itself is pure/synchronous and stateless (pure functions over a PipelineGraph; no shared mutable state, no async). The only process-level shared state is module-import-time registry population: NODE_REGISTRY is a module-global dict filled as a side effect of importing _builders then _codegen_builders, guarded by ensure_registry_ready()'s _REGISTRY_READY flag and validate_registry_complete(); duplicate registrations raise. PipelineGraph carries @cached_property memos (node_map, parents_of, _haute_base_fingerprint) and overrides model_copy to invalidate them — relevant because graphs are evolved immutably elsewhere and codegen reads .nodes/.edges/.submodels. The transactional concurrency/atomicity concerns (rollback, self-write markers, stale-config deletion) live in the caller SavePipelineService, not in codegen.
perf_characteristics: Linear in nodes+edges; dominated by string formatting + repeated ast.parse/tokenize passes. Notable repeated work: _inject_contract_kwarg runs a full tokenize.generate_tokens scan of each node's emitted code per node; _assert_emitted_files_parse ast.parse's each whole file once at the end; graph_to_code_multi re-validates and re-model_validates submodel raw nodes multiple times (collision pass, per-submodel emit, root id_to_func map). _format_contract_kwarg for MODEL_SCORE may trigger an MLflow artifact load to discover feature names at codegen time (network/disk); infra failures are caught and downgraded to contract="opaque" (ConfigError still propagates). load_contract_cached / model load are stat-gated/cached on the exec side. For typical pipelines (tens of nodes) this is sub-second; cost scales with submodel count and node code size, not data volume.
invariants: Generated code must be valid Python — _assert_emitted_files_parse ast.parse's every file before write; a SyntaxError aborts the (transactional) save (codegen.py:819-843).

Save/parse round-trip is a fixpoint: re-saving an unchanged pipeline must produce the same graph. Drives _sanitize_description (docstring round-trip), _safe_str/_safe_path quoting, _code_extraction boilerplate stripping, and contract sorting.

Generated body preserves intended pricing semantics by calling the SAME runtime helpers the executor uses (apply_banding_from_config / apply_rating_step_from_config / score_from_config / execute_edge_join / load_v2_api_source). Bodies and exec builders must not drift.

_sanitize_func_name is injective enough that distinct node labels never collide to one identifier; collisions are a HARD ParseError (codegen.py:549-594) because two `def <name>` blocks would silently shadow. Must stay byte-identical to frontend sanitizeName.ts.
NODE_REGISTRY has exactly one exec AND one codegen builder per NodeType (validate_registry_complete); a missing builder raises KeyError rather than silently falling back to _gen_transform.
Contract emitted in `contract=...` must equal the runtime-enforced contract; column sets are sorted for determinism; opaque is the string sentinel 'opaque'.

edgeJoin sources are emitted in [base, join] role order resolved from config (baseInput/joinInput) against connected node ids; role kwargs name emitted func names, not raw canvas node ids (codegen.py:427-445, _codegen_builders.py:1048-1091).
Config-folder node types emit `config="config/<folder>/<func_name>.json"` and the sidecar path is path-traversal-guarded (config_path_for_node rejects '..'/separators).

User-controlled text (labels, descriptions, port names, column names, paths) is always escaped before landing in source — never bare f-string interpolation into Python (connect ports use json.dumps; strings use _safe_str).

Submodel cross-boundary edges MUST carry well-formed `in__<child_id>` / `out__<child_id>` handles pointing at real children, else ParseError; the SUBMODEL/SUBMODEL_PORT placeholders never reach codegen dispatch (they raise).
Codegen output paths are restricted by the caller to the main source_file or modules/<name>.py (no traversal/absolute/symlink escape) — SavePipelineService._validate_output_rel_path.
Misconfiguration (e.g. modelScore sourceType='run' with empty run_id) fails loud at save time; only environmental/infra failures degrade to opaque contract.

region: Execution engine (run generated code over Polars; lazy plan; chunking; admission; dataframe execution cache)
purpose: Executes a React-Flow pipeline graph as a real Polars pipeline (no saved .py needed) across multiple strategies: (1) eager single-pass execution with a process-global, byte-bounded preview cache for interactive preview/trace, capping source rows; (2) fully lazy plan construction with adaptive parquet/collect checkpoints for batch sinks, deploy scoring, training and optimiser setup so Polars optimises the full plan end-to-end; (3) a fail-loud chunked map-reduce runner that only executes graphs with a proven ChunkPlan (row-local whitelist); plus profile-aware admission (per-profile memory budgets + process-wide in-flight reservation) and a parquet-backed, lineage-keyed dataframe execution cache for reusing materialized intermediate frames across runs. Memory safety and cooperative cancellation are threaded through an ExecutionContext.

internal_dataflow:
IN: a PipelineGraph (nodes+edges+preamble+source_file) plus a target_node_id, source/scenario, row_limit and an optional ExecutionContext.

PREVIEW PATH (execute_graph): canonicalises paths via projection.prepare_graph indirectly; computes a graph_fingerprint that folds in row_limit, source, enforce_contracts flag, preview-projection cache suffix, and runtime_input_extra_keys (file/json-cache state) so out-of-band input changes invalidate entries. Looks up module-global _preview_cache (FingerprintCache, 64MB default, byte-bounded on 'eager_outputs'). On full hit serves cached DataFrames; on partial hit it re-runs _eager_execute and MERGES fresh outputs over previous (fresh wins on overlap), pins the merged entry; on miss runs _eager_execute and pins. _eager_execute compiles the preamble (_compile_preamble) then calls _execute_eager_core which: prepares/topo-sorts the graph (pruning live-switch branches for the source), re-validates graph-shape contracts on the executed subset, builds per-node funcs (_build_funcs->_build_node_fn), then walks topo order. For each node: resolves per-edge parent frames via _pick_source_frame (multi-port apiInput dict routing by sourceHandle), adds Polars .cache() on parents feeding >1 consumer (diamond reuse), enforces input/output column contracts via collect_schema(), applies selected_columns then column_renames, projects to needed columns, and materialises via streaming_collect (allow_broad only for PREVIEW_EAGER profile). Results become NodeResult dicts (preview rows bounded by PREVIEW_MAX_CELLS/column_count).

LAZY PATH (execute_sink / _execute_lazy): resolves graph paths, prepares graph, optionally seeds outputs from the DataFrameExecutionCache (validating that each provided cache key matches a freshly recomputed expected key + policy fingerprint + source + profile, rejecting hits missing required columns), computes a backward projection plan, builds funcs for only uncovered nodes, then walks topo order producing LazyFrames. Adaptive checkpointing (_checkpoint_decision) sinks fan-out/join/join-feeder nodes to temp parquet (projected to needed cols) and replaces them with scan_parquet to break Polars plan duplication and chained-join memory accumulation (#24206); MODEL_SCORE in batch is skipped (already self-checkpoints). Consumed parent LazyFrames are deleted when their remaining-consumer count hits zero; gc.collect()+_malloc_trim() every _GC_BATCH_INTERVAL(3) checkpoints. Selected nodes may be materialized into the dataframe cache via materialize_lazy_frame_with_cache (bounded_sink to parquet, store_artifact, scan back). execute_sink finally streams the sink via bounded_sink (no eager fallback) and counts rows via scan + streaming_collect; temp checkpoint dir is rmtree'd in finally.

CHUNK PATH (chunk_plan -> iter_chunked_frames): chunk_plan proves eligibility (exactly one flat-file parquet/csv dataSource root unless start_frame supplied; single-parent chunk suffix; per-node ChunkCapability from a registry; row-local user code via AST whitelist) and computes chunk_size (explicit rows or byte-budget derived from sampled column widths) and a row_expansion_factor for scenario expanders. iter_chunked_frames streams source batches via bounded_collect_batches(maintain_order=True), runs the single-parent chain per batch applying selected_columns/renames/projection, streaming_collect's each target chunk to a bounded DataFrame, optionally writes a per-chunk parquet checkpoint, and yields ChunkBatch. run_chunked_reduce funnels into a bounded reducer; collect_chunked is opt-in unbounded.

ADMISSION: create_admitted_execution_context resolves a per-profile ExecutionBudget (env override > adaptive-local fraction of available RAM with OS reserve > fixed default), samples current RSS, refuses if RSS already exceeds a process RSS cap, reserves a share of a process-wide in-flight memory budget (_IN_FLIGHT_RESERVATIONS under _IN_FLIGHT_LOCK), and builds an ExecutionContext whose checkpoint()/stage() sample RSS, raise on cancellation, raise ExecutionMemoryLimitExceededError on budget breach, and emit memory-pressure events at 50/75/90%. weakref.finalize releases the in-flight reservation when the context is GC'd.

OUT: NodeResult dict (preview), SinkResponse (rows+path+metrics), ChunkBatch stream, or cache-backed LazyFrames; plus ExecutionMetrics payloads.
concurrency_model:
Designed for a multi-threaded FastAPI server (preview, trace, estimate, train, optimiser, deploy can run concurrently in threads of one process). Several pieces of process-global shared state:
- executor._preview_cache: a single module-global FingerprintCache shared by ALL requests and by trace.py. Internally guarded by an RLock, with pin/unpin and byte-bounded LRU eviction. execute_graph performs a NON-atomic try_get -> _eager_execute -> store/pin sequence; two concurrent requests on the same fingerprint can both miss/extend and both store, last-writer-wins (extend path explicitly merges, fresh wins on overlap). Pin is held across result serialization and released in a finally.
- executor._compile_preamble_cached: functools.lru_cache (own C-level lock) but all MISSES additionally hold a single global threading.Lock _preamble_lock for the whole sys.path reprioritisation + sys.modules eviction + exec window (sys.path/sys.modules are process-global). lru_cache HITS bypass _preamble_lock.
- _polars_utils.temporary_streaming_chunk_size mutates process-global pl.Config under _STREAMING_CHUNK_SIZE_LOCK (save/load) — concurrent batch jobs serialise on this lock and the global chunk size is shared for the scope's duration.
- _execution_admission in-flight reservation: _IN_FLIGHT_RESERVATIONS dict + _IN_FLIGHT_COUNTER under _IN_FLIGHT_LOCK (RLock); released via a thread-safe idempotent closure and weakref.finalize.
- DataFrameExecutionCache: per-instance _lock (from LRUCache) for entry maps, a separate _materialize_locks_guard guarding a WeakValueDictionary of per-key RLocks (materialization_lock serialises same-key writes), _scan_refcounts and _store_pins for artifact lifetime. Scan LazyFrames register weakref.finalize callbacks that call back into the cache to decrement refcounts and possibly unlink the parquet artifact — finalizers can run on arbitrary threads at GC time.
- ExecutionContext is shared across worker threads of one run: metrics recorder is RLock-guarded; per-thread stage stacks via threading.local; memory-pressure dedup set under its own RLock; admission release idempotent under a lock. A single context's stage()/_CURRENT_EXECUTION_CONTEXT contextvar is set/reset per-thread.
Within a single execution the eager/lazy walks are SERIAL (topo order, one node at a time); the chunk runner is explicitly serial with exactly one in-flight chunk (plan.serial and max_in_flight_chunks==1 enforced).
invariants: Preview cache fingerprint uniquely identifies the materialized content: graph_fingerprint folds in graph structure, row_limit, source, enforce_contracts, preview-projection suffix, and runtime_input_extra_keys (file mtime/size/content-hash + json-cache state). Any input change MUST produce a new key or stale frames are served.

DataFrameExecutionCacheKey uniquely identifies a reusable materialized frame: lineage_fingerprint (upstream-only subgraph), namespace, node_id, source, semantic profile, input_fingerprint, required_columns, extra_keys, execution_policy_fingerprint. On hit, _execute_lazy re-derives the expected key and rejects any mismatch (source/profile/policy/key) — a provided key must equal a freshly computed one.

A cache hit that lacks any required column must be rejected (not silently served), and a materialization whose frame lacks required columns must be skipped — required_columns is a hard containment contract.

Parquet checkpoint/dataframe-cache artifacts must be created atomically (atomic_write temp-then-rename) and unlinked on any failure; the temp .parquet.tmp must never be left behind. execute_sink's join-checkpoint temp dir is always rmtree'd.

A cached parquet artifact's file must outlive every LazyFrame derived from its scan: the artifact is unlinked only after the last scan refcount is released AND the entry is evicted/replaced. Callers MUST keep the source scan reference alive while composing derived frames (cache-backed nodes are explicitly NOT released by _release_consumed_parents).

A just-stored cache entry must survive its own insertion and the gap until first scan pins it: while materialization_lock/_store_pins is held the key is never an eviction victim (store-window exemption), mirroring the preview/trace 'just-stored is MRU' rule.

Bounded-memory execution paths must never silently broaden to an eager full collect: streaming_collect/bounded_sink/bounded_collect_batches raise BoundedMemoryUnsupportedError unless allow_broad=True, which is permitted ONLY for the PREVIEW_EAGER profile.

Chunked execution must be provably equivalent to full execution: only nodes/user-code admitted by the AST row-local whitelist (each backed by a chunked==full property proof) and the ChunkCapability registry may run chunked; unsupported shapes raise ChunkPlanUnsupportedError and callers fall back to the always-correct full executor. The whitelist rejects any frame reference that is not a method-chain receiver and any cross-row operation (group_by/sort/join/collect/strategy fills/column-haystack is_in).
Source row order must be preserved across chunk boundaries for map-only plans (bounded_collect_batches maintain_order=True; capabilities declare preserves_row_order).

Column contracts (Contract.inputs/outputs) are enforced at every node boundary on both eager and lazy paths via collect_schema(); a ContractMismatchError always raises even in swallow_errors/preview mode. Passthrough/stub-wired nodes are exempt from the OUTPUT check only.
Sink output path resolution must stay inside project_root when project_root is supplied (server route): is_relative_to(root) or ValueError — the sandbox containment boundary.
ChunkPlan must match the prepared graph it executes against: tuple(prepared.order) == plan.node_ids, else ChunkPlanUnsupportedError (guards against graph drift between planning and running).

Resolved memory budgets and in-flight reservations are positive integers; available_ram_bytes() and env values must be positive or RuntimeError. The in-flight reservation sum must never exceed the process in-flight limit at admission time.

The preamble compile cache key must distinguish different utility-file contents when refresh is requested (execution_fingerprint), and pipeline_dir is normalised to str so Path/str produce identical lru_cache keys. Dangerous module bindings (os/sys/subprocess/...) are stripped from the compiled preamble namespace.

Multi-port apiInput sources emit dict[port,frame]; such a bundle must never be cache-materialized as a single node (raises) and downstream edges must route by sourceHandle (null sourceHandle on a multi-port edge raises).

Variable-width columns (strings/lists) are estimated at a fixed 64 bytes when not sampled, and only the chunk_start source is sampled (intermediate expansions use estimates).

Worth verifying against the memory budget the admission layer enforces.

candidate_risks.concern: DataFrameExecutionCache artifact lifetime hinges on weakref.finalize on scan LazyFrames calling _release_pinned_scan to decrement _scan_refcounts and unlink the parquet. If a derived/cached LazyFrame keeps the scan alive longer than expected, or a finalizer runs late, the artifact may be unlinked while a downstream collect still needs it (or never unlinked, leaking disk). _release_consumed_parents deliberately keeps cache_backed nodes, but the coupling between Python GC timing and Polars Rust buffers is subtle.
candidate_risks.why: Premature unlink -> FileNotFoundError on a later streaming collect (run-failing); delayed/missing finalize -> unbounded temp-dir growth. Both are intermittent and GC-timing dependent (silent until it bites). Windows file-sharing (PermissionError on unlink while open) is explicitly acknowledged elsewhere.

candidate_risks.concern: In-flight memory admission reserves budget.memory_limit_bytes (the configured/adaptive LIMIT, not actual or estimated usage) and is released via weakref.finalize(context, release). If a caller forgets to close()/drop the context promptly, reservations linger until GC, so the process-wide in-flight budget can be exhausted by stale reservations and legitimately-sized new jobs are refused with in_flight_memory_budget_exceeded.
candidate_risks.why: Could cause spurious admission refusals (availability bug) or, conversely, since reservations are coarse LIMIT-sized rather than usage-tracked, admit work that collectively overcommits real RAM. Concurrency/resource-accounting class.

candidate_risks.concern: ExecutionContext memory budget is enforced only at explicit checkpoint()/stage() boundaries by sampling process RSS. A single node's streaming_collect or a Polars operation that balloons memory between two checkpoints is not interrupted; the limit is a coarse post-hoc gate, and adaptive budgets are derived from available RAM at admission time (can be stale by execution time).

invariants: Projection NEVER silently drops a column a node needs: any node/edge whose ownership cannot be proven keeps a FULL-WIDTH (None) boundary (_unprojected_boundary_demands, opaque contracts, cross/full/right joins, dynamic join how/suffix, ambiguous renames) so execution fails loudly on a real missing-column error rather than the planner manufacturing a misleading one.

Generated/user code preserves source pricing semantics under projection: source post-load code is only treated as projection-transparent for a whitelisted set of row-only ops (limit/head/tail/slice) that neither read nor create columns (source_user_code_preserves_column_projection); anything else forces a full-width source scan (_must_run_source_user_code_unprojected).

Rename-bearing / select-bearing / derived-reference single-parent Polars code is analysed in PROVABLE EXECUTION ORDER (_ordered_expression_demands) because the unordered union walk would re-add post-rename/derived names to the parent demand (over-demand) or intersect select outputs with downstream demand (under-demand); unprovable shapes stay full-width.

Polars applies rename pairs simultaneously: demand is translated through the reverse mapping and any swap collision / removed-name demand returns None (full width) rather than a wrong projection (_demand_before_rename).

projection_rule_coverage must mention EVERY NodeType exactly once, keyed correctly, with non-empty rules; opaque types must carry the opaque_contract rule — validated at import time (validate_projection_rule_coverage / module-level call).

graph_fingerprint uniquely identifies execution-relevant content: node configs (canonical_json) + full port-aware edge wiring + preamble + imported utility file content + ALGO_VERSION prefix; a canonicalisation change must bump ALGO_VERSION to avoid stale-cache collisions.

Trace cache key == preview-compatible key material: trace fp = graph_fingerprint(graph, target, '<row_limit>:<source>', *runtime_extra_keys); preview reuse keys reconstruct executor.py's exact preview keys (base '<row_limit>:<source>:contracts=<int>' plus optional projection suffix). The runtime_input_extra_keys are computed ONCE and shared so one trace observes one input state.

Trace is a PURE OBSERVATION layer: it never mutates the execution pipeline; it reuses the same materialised DataFrames the user saw and post-hoc correlates rows by value, guaranteeing displayed lineage == preview data.

Preview reuse only when the FULL ancestor chain is present and non-None (preview uses swallow_errors=True / target-only caching); partial caches fall through to a cold full execution so the waterfall stays truthful.

Row correlation prefers AMBIGUITY-REJECTION over guessing: exact match on all shared columns wins; otherwise the single widest relaxed subset wins; competing best rows return (None,-1) and the step is omitted (never silently row 0). Edge-join JOIN-role (right) parents must not relax (_allows_relaxed_parent_match).

Edge-join correlation routes suffixed/colliding columns to the correct parent: Polars keeps the BASE copy under the original name and emits the right copy as <col><suffix>; _edge_join_right_match_row matches the right parent on <col>/keys, never on left-row values.

Waterfall arithmetic is value-derived (delta = value_after - value_before; implied factor value_after/value_before) and must RECONCILE within float tolerance with the traced output value; expression text only selects x/+ label and can never corrupt numbers. A violation raises WaterfallReconciliationError -> structured {error} payload, never a silently wrong chart (CODE_REVIEW.md C8).

Trace JSON-safe boundary: integers beyond MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (2^53-1) are stringified (_jsonify_row/to_json_safe); the waterfall refuses to render JS-unsafe integers as numbers (WaterfallUnavailableError) rather than lose precision.

Enrichment matched/default flags cannot diverge from the runtime rating join because keys are compared in the engine's canonical form (normalise_rating_key) and the entry walk mirrors the runtime keep='last' dedup by iterating reversed(entries).

Trace cache bounded by retained BYTES (size-sensitive slot 'eager_outputs', estimator shared with preview cache) and entry count, LRU eviction, oversized single entry rejected at store time with a loud log while the trace itself still succeeds.

candidate_risks.concern: Broad try/except swallowing across the entire enrichment pipeline could mask genuine lineage corruption as a benign per-step 'error' annotation.
candidate_risks.why: enrich_steps wraps every stage (expression parse/eval, chain, input_sources, rename, node detail, row lineage) and the whole step body in try/except that logs a WARNING and writes an {error} marker, then continues. This is deliberate (a single bad step must not poison the whole trace) but it sits in tension with the repo's 'fail loudly, no band-aid fallbacks' rule: a systematic enricher bug (e.g. wrong column) would silently degrade EVERY trace to error-annotated steps that the UI may render as 'no expression detected', and the values shown still come from correlation. Worth auditing which failures are truly non-fatal vs. which hide wrong numbers.

candidate_risks.concern: Fast-path positional row match with NO shared columns trusts position for any equal-row-count parent, which can attach the wrong upstream row after a non-1:1 transform that happens to preserve row count.
candidate_risks.why: _correlate_rows_posthoc fast path: when len(parent_df)==child_len and there are no shared columns between the projected match_row and the candidate (e.g. a full rename or select that drops all matchable names), it accepts the positionally-aligned row as correct for '1:1 transforms'. But equal row count does not prove a 1:1 positional mapping (a sort, a join that preserves cardinality, or a filter+concat could keep the count while reordering). This is a silent-correctness lineage risk: the trace could show a different row's values as the parent contribution.

candidate_risks.concern: _fix_upstream_values re-correlates upstream rows by float equality with a fixed absolute tolerance (1e-6), which can mis-match small-magnitude or large-magnitude values.
candidate_risks.why: When an upstream step shows null but expression evaluation produced a known value, the code relocates the source row via df.filter((pl.col(c)-known).abs() < 1e-6). A fixed 1e-6 ABSOLUTE tolerance is scale-dependent: for premiums in the millions it is far too tight (legit equal values differ by float noise > 1e-6 only rarely, but rounding through JSON can), and for tiny factors near 1e-7 it is too loose (distinct values collide). A wrong match overwrites the step's output_values with another row's cell — silently wrong lineage. The surrounding logic is opportunistic patching of correlation misses, amplifying the blast radius if it matches the wrong row.

candidate_risks.concern: Trace and preview FingerprintCaches share mutable DataFrame values across threads; try_get returns a shallow copy whose inner frames are shared by design, and trace mutates step output_values built from those frames.
candidate_risks.why: FingerprintCache.try_get copies only the top-level slot dict; eager_outputs DataFrames are shared. With HAUTE_TRACE_MAX_CONCURRENCY>1 (default 2) two concurrent traces over the same fingerprint read the same cached frame objects. Polars frames are immutable so reads are safe, but _fix_upstream_values mutates the per-step output_values dict (Python-side, derived via .row()), not the frame — so likely safe. The lead worth auditing: confirm no code path mutates a cached DataFrame in place, and that the cross-cache reuse (preview cache injected into trace) never has the trace evict/replace a preview entry the executor still relies on.

candidate_risks.concern: PolarsFanInRule passthrough-parent inference (simple_left_join_passthrough_parent / unambiguous_passthrough_parent) assigns leftover demanded columns to a single inferred parent; an incorrect inference would route a real column to the wrong parent edge.
candidate_risks.why: When declared inputs_by_parent does not cover all base_contribution columns, the rule tries to attribute 'missing' columns to a passthrough parent inferred from simple left/semi/anti joins or from the sole parent whose declaration is a subset of referenced. If the heuristic picks the wrong parent (e.g. a left join chain it parsed incompletely, or aliasing it could not resolve), the edge projection demands the column from a parent that doesn't produce it -> at best a loud failure, at worst (if that parent coincidentally has the column) a semantically wrong narrow read. Multi-parent Polars projection is the most intricate path here and deserves targeted adversarial tests.

candidate_risks.concern: parse_expression / _compute_result use 'last with_columns match wins' for the target column and a best-effort AST evaluator; the evaluator's result can silently diverge from Polars semantics, feeding the displayed calculation (not the waterfall numbers).
candidate_risks.why: _ExprEvaluator reimplements arithmetic/conditional/horizontal-func semantics in Python over JSON-coerced row values. Subtle divergences (integer vs float division, null propagation rules, when/then branch selection, string coercion) produce a 'substituted_text'/'result_value' shown to the user as the calculation. These are display-only (the waterfall reconciles against observed values), but a wrong displayed formula result undermines the explainability product. The parser also returns an opaque expression on ANY exception (never raises), so silent degradation is the designed behaviour. Worth a focused review of evaluator vs Polars on edge ops.

candidate_risks.concern: execute_trace Python default row_limit=1000 vs TraceRequest schema default row_limit=100 means a direct (CLI/test) caller will never reuse the route-warmed preview cache, and a trace at a different row_limit than the preview observes a DIFFERENT row sample.
candidate_risks.why: Both the trace cache key and the preview-reuse keys embed row_limit. The route always forwards body.row_limit (default 100, matching preview), so the GUI path is consistent. But the divergent in-code defaults are a latent inconsistency: anyone calling execute_trace directly gets 1000, forcing cold execution and — more importantly — correlating against the first 1000 source rows while the user's preview showed 100, so a clicked row could correlate to a different upstream row if source ordering is unstable. candidate_risks.concern: Single-column-lineage guard rejects multi-branch origins, but relies on schema_diff columns_added/modified which are derived from JSON-coerced single-row values; a value that coerces equal across branches could under-report a modification and let a cross-branch waterfall through.
candidate_risks.why: _ensure_single_column_lineage and the waterfall step loop key off schema_diff.columns_modified, which _compute_schema_diff computes by comparing JSON-safe input vs output cell values (with NaN==NaN). If a genuine modification leaves the single traced cell numerically unchanged (e.g. a no-op for this row but a real op generally), the step is treated as passthrough and contributes nothing; conversely float/JSON coercion could mark spurious modifications. Because the final cumulative must reconcile, a truly wrong chart usually fails loudly — but a missing contribution that still reconciles (identity step) would silently omit a node from the explanation.

candidate_risks.concern: compute_prepared_plan multi-consumer seed handling: when a node has >1 child and demand is opaque, a non-strict profile silently DROPS the caller's projection seed instead of applying or failing.
candidate_risks.why: In compute_prepared_plan, if needed[node] is None (opaque from multiple downstream consumers) and a seed exists, strict profiles raise ProjectionImpossibleError, but non-strict profiles fall through leaving needed[node]=None — the seed is ignored. This is defensible (can't narrow below opaque from multiple consumers) but means a caller-supplied required-columns seed can be silently no-op'd in non-strict (e.g. preview) profiles; a reviewer should confirm no caller depends on the seed taking effect there.

concurrency_model: FastAPI async routes offload blocking work to threads. Trace and preview each have an asyncio.Semaphore (HAUTE_TRACE_MAX_CONCURRENCY / HAUTE_PREVIEW_MAX_CONCURRENCY, default 2) plus a SupersessionCoordinator that runs only the latest request per (operation, source_file, source, fingerprint, params) key and 409s superseded ones. The core engines (execute_trace, compute_prepared_plan) are synchronous and run under run_blocking_with_response_timeout. Shared mutable state: module-level FingerprintCache singletons — trace.py::_cache and executor.py::_preview_cache — backed by LRUCache with an RLock guarding all operations; the trace is injected the preview cache (PreviewReader) so two caches' DataFrame values are shared. Polars frames are immutable, so concurrent reads are safe; per-step Python dicts (output_values) are mutated only on freshly-correlated copies, not on cached frames. graph_fingerprint uses a request-scoped GraphFingerprintMemo (explicitly documented as not thread-shared). No locks are held across the cross-module preview->trace cache reuse, which is the main concurrency surface to audit.
internal_dataflow: PROJECTION: ProjectionRequest(graph, target, profile, required_columns_by_node, source) -> plan() -> prepare_graph (prune live-switch edges -> ancestors filter -> topo order -> parents_of) -> compute_prepared_plan reverse-topo sweep. For each node in reversed(order): accumulate child demand -> apply caller seed / AllExcept / source-full-width override -> route via parent_demands_for_node (optimiser/single-parent-polars) else opaque/edge-join/fan-in rules else generic contract algebra base_contribution=(needed-produced)|referenced. Produces ProjectionPlan{needed_by_node, edge_demands, opaque_boundaries, diagnostics}. _execute_lazy consumes it to apply per-edge projection and may augment it at runtime via with_runtime_inferred_streaming_edges for inferred simple joins. TRACE: route trace_row -> flatten_graph -> execute_trace. Compute trace fingerprint (graph + 'row_limit:source' + runtime_extra_keys). Cache hit -> reuse (eager_outputs, order, parents_of, node_map, source_ids). Miss -> _materialize_eager_outputs: try injected preview cache (reconstruct executor preview keys incl. projection suffix) and reuse only if full ancestor chain present, else cold _execute_eager_core(swallow_errors=False). Store in trace cache. Then: verify clicked row_values match target row (relocate via _find_target_row_index or raise 409); _correlate_rows_posthoc walks backward, value-matching each parent's row (edge-join-aware) into cached_rows; _assemble_steps builds TraceStep[] with SchemaDiff; enrich_steps populates expression/calculation/node_detail/row_lineage (recursive input_sources + _fix_upstream_values mutation); _prune_to_column_relevance trims to column-contributing nodes; build_waterfall_from_steps derives reconciled contributions. trace_result_to_dict -> to_json_safe -> TraceResponse JSON -> frontend useTracing/TracePanel.
perf_characteristics: Trace is cache-first: first click pays full eager materialisation (model-score nodes ~1s on ~678K rows per the docstring); subsequent clicks that change only row_index/column hit the trace cache (<10ms) or reuse the preview cache. Caches are bounded by retained bytes (default = PREVIEW_CACHE_MAX_BYTES via HAUTE_TRACE_CACHE_MAX_BYTES) using Polars estimated_size, plus an entry-count bound (default 8); LRU eviction, just-stored entry is MRU. Row correlation cost: the fast positional path is O(shared_cols) per node; the value-matching fallback builds a per-row equality matrix O(rows x shared_cols) via Polars select (_match_columns_by_row_index) — bounded by row_limit (default 100 from the GUI). Projection planning is a single O(nodes+edges) reverse-topo pass with per-node AST parses of user code (each ast.parse is the dominant cost for Polars-heavy graphs). Optimiser-apply enrichment batches trace match in 50K-row chunks. Concurrency capped at 2 with supersession to shed superseded GUI requests.

purpose: Owns cache identity, integrity, and invalidation for the pricing engine's preview/trace/dataframe-execution caches plus the v2 per-port JSON apiInput cache. Three concerns layered: (1) graph fingerprinting — deterministic content-addressed digests of pipeline-graph execution inputs (node configs, edge wiring, preamble, imported utility module, data-file signatures) used as cache keys; (2) in-memory cache machinery — a thread-safe bounded LRU with pinning/TTL/byte-budgets (LRUCache), its multi-slot subclass (FingerprintCache), a stat-gated single-flight artifact cache, and a parquet-backed dataframe-execution cache; (3) on-disk data ingest — the v2 JSON-shred codec (one parquet per emit-true table) with its dual working/committed cache layout, atomic build/swap, corruption/partial-write handling, and the config sidecar read/write path. Central invariant the whole region defends: a cache key uniquely and deterministically identifies the content it caches, and any input change (schema, data bytes, wiring, code) is observed so stale results are never served.

invariants: Single canonical encoder: every byte of JSON-shaped digest material in the codebase must come from _cache.canonical_json (mappings need string keys & sort by code point; lists/tuples in order; sets ordered by (type-tag,value); non-finite floats -> deterministic Infinity/NaN tokens; everything else raises TypeError, never repr()). Two encoders = silent cache collisions (the v5 ALGO bump exists precisely to retire a divergent encoder).

ALGO_VERSION is embedded as a 'v<N>:' prefix on every graph_fingerprint output so a canonicalisation change can never collide with stale entries; it is read dynamically each call so a bump (or monkeypatch) invalidates all fingerprint-keyed entries in one step. DATAFRAME_EXECUTION_CACHE_VERSION need not bump on an ALGO bump because the payload embeds the prefixed lineage_fingerprint.

A cache key uniquely and deterministically identifies its cached content: same graph+params -> same key across processes/runs (no hash-seed/insertion-order dependence); any node-config/edge-wiring/preamble/utility-content/data-file change -> different key.

Edge wiring is digest material INCLUDING sourceHandle/targetHandle (which port feeds a consumer); the absent handle (null) stays distinct from every real handle string including ports literally named 'None'/'null' (v4 port-aware change).

graph_fingerprint lineage scoping: dataframe_execution_cache_key fingerprints only the target node's upstream subgraph, so downstream edits don't churn upstream entries while any upstream change produces a new key.

Data-file freshness: a built JSON cache is valid only if meta.json schema_fingerprint matches the v2 schema AND the recorded data_file signature (size+mtime_ns, sha256 arbitrating an mtime-only drift) still matches the file on disk AND a parquet exists for every emitting table. A pre-W2 meta with no data_file signature is stale by construction.

The v2 build is serialized per canonical cache directory (one lock per normcased resolved path) and atomic: written into a unique sibling temp dir then swapped into place, with the old dir restored if the second rename fails — an interrupted/failed build can never corrupt a valid cache or leave a half-written one.
Per-frame parquet schema is co-located in the parquet footer key-value metadata so each file is self-describing (no schema-wrote-but-data-failed race).

table_is_emitting (emit AND >=1 selected column) is THE single emitting predicate shared by build/validity/load — disagreement previously wedged the cache permanently (build skipped a parquet that validity demanded).

Zero silent record loss: every top-level non-object input (skipped_records) and every shape-mismatched array element at an emitting table's depth (skipped_rows_by_table) is counted into ShredSkipStats, written to meta.json, and surfaced in build/status responses.
Strict typing on parquet build fails loud & column-specific; bool-into-numeric and int/bool-into-date are explicitly rejected (Polars would silently coerce True->1 or 2024->1975-07-18).
committed/ mirror gating: save promotes working/ -> committed/ only if THIS process built working/ this session (_session_consulted_hashes), guarding against promoting a stale cross-session working/.

Path sandbox: config_path_for_node / load_node_config / resolve_runtime_file_path reject path-traversal and paths that escape the project/config root; the cache routes resolve with enforce_project_root=True. cache identity (_path_hash) is the SHA-256 of the canonical absolute resolved path, stable across cwd/relative-vs-absolute.

Cache-key material vs JSON-safety are separate: canonical_json is digest material (compact, ASCII, deterministic NaN tokens); _json_safe.to_json_safe is the API-wire contract (>2^53 ints -> strings, non-finite floats -> sentinel objects) and must not be conflated.

candidate_risks.concern: _v2_fingerprint silently `continue`s past any non-dict table or non-dict column instead of failing/encoding them, so a malformed-but-present table fingerprints identically to its absence (and to a different malformed table).
candidate_risks.why: Two structurally different on-disk configs can collide to the same schema_fingerprint, defeating the no-op trapdoor and cache-validity check — a stale cache could be judged fresh. validate_v2_schema would reject these on the build path, but is_per_port_cache_valid / mirror_cache_to_committed compare fingerprints of arbitrary on-disk configs without re-validating.

candidate_risks.concern: cache_state_signature_for_graph keys preview/trace invalidation on int(meta.json st_mtime*1000), but many filesystems (and the value source) give second-or-coarser mtime resolution; two cache builds within the same second/tick can yield an identical signature.
candidate_risks.why: If a JSON cache is rebuilt with new content but meta.json's mtime bucket is unchanged, dependent preview/trace entries keyed partly on this signature may not invalidate, serving stale previews. The data_file-signature path inside is_per_port_cache_valid is finer, but the preview-cache key relies on this mtime fragment.

candidate_risks.concern: _BUILD_LOCKS and _session_consulted_hashes are unbounded process-global dicts/sets keyed by resolved cache path; combined with the per-cache build lock, the mirror gate, and the executor's separate FingerprintCache/DataFrameExecutionCache locks there are multiple independent lock domains touching the same on-disk cache.
candidate_risks.why: Build serialization protects same-dir interleaving, but mirror_cache_to_committed (called from the save pipeline) takes NO build lock while it reads working/meta + copytrees working/ -> committed/; a concurrent build swapping working/ during a mirror could copy a torn mix (build swap is atomic at the dir level, but copytree walks files individually).

candidate_risks.concern: mirror_cache_to_committed's atomic swap removes a `.old` backup with shutil.rmtree(ignore_errors=True) and uses copytree+rename, but unlike _json_shred._swap_dir_into_place it does not use the Windows PermissionError rename-retry; a transient handle lock on committed/ during rename raises and leaves committed/ as the restored backup.
candidate_risks.why: On Windows (a documented target — see _rename_dir_with_retry) a save could intermittently fail to promote to committed/, and the rollback path itself (backup.rename(committed_dir)) is also unretried, risking committed/ left missing if that rename also hits a lock.

candidate_risks.concern: _v2_fingerprint excludes the apiInput `path`/`contract` and includes row_id_column but NOT displayPath/status/levels-vs-selected subtleties; meanwhile inference emits status='Inferred' and the editor sets 'Confirmed'. The fingerprint deliberately omits status, but `levels` IS included — a change to a column's categorical levels invalidates the shred cache even though levels don't affect shred output.
candidate_risks.why: Including levels over-invalidates (extra rebuild churn, harmless), but the asymmetry signals the fingerprint field-set was chosen by hand; any future field that DOES affect shred output but is omitted would silently serve stale parquets. Worth auditing the field set against what build_per_port_cache actually reads.

candidate_risks.concern: _resolve_leaf treats a list encountered mid dotted-leaf walk as its first element (cur[0]) 'degenerate but consistent with v1'; _coerce_scalar widens int->float for scalar arrays but leaves a Python int that overflows Int64 to fail only at _buffer_to_frame.
candidate_risks.why: First-element-of-list resolution can silently pick an arbitrary value when source data has an unexpected array at a leaf, producing a plausible-but-wrong cached column with no skip accounting (skip stats only count array elements at table depth, not silently-collapsed leaf lists).

candidate_risks.concern: Multiple layers (StatGatedCache, GraphFingerprintMemo, _data_file_matches fast path, cache_state_signature) gate on (mtime_ns,size) or (path,mtime,size) and explicitly accept that a byte change preserving both mtime and size is below resolution.
candidate_risks.why: A deploy tool / editor that rewrites identical-size content while preserving mtime (rsync --times, some copy tools) would serve stale cached values. _data_file_matches mitigates via sha256 only when mtime DIFFERS; if mtime is preserved it returns fresh without hashing. This is documented as an accepted trade but is a real silent-correctness boundary across the whole region.

candidate_risks.concern: DataFrameExecutionCache defers parquet unlink to weakref.finalize(lazy_frame) of consumer scans, with scan refcounts + store-window pins + base pins composed across overrides of _is_pinned/_remove_key/_release_scan; the artifact filename appends uuid4 to the key-hash so replacement creates a new file relying on the release path to unlink the orphan.
candidate_risks.why: Highly intricate ownership: an incorrect refcount/pin transition could either unlink a parquet still referenced by a live LazyFrame (CacheArtifactCorrupt/Missing on collect) or leak parquet files in root forever. The _release_scan single-unlink rule depends on entry_before/entry_after path identity comparisons that are easy to get subtly wrong under replacement races.

candidate_risks.concern: preamble_imports_utility falls back to substring 'utility' in preamble on SyntaxError, and _utility_candidates_for_dir hashes utility.py/utility/ under pipeline_dir AND cwd; a preamble that imports utility but whose nearby utility files differ from the actually-imported module (sys.path differences) could fingerprint the wrong files.
candidate_risks.why: If the executed utility module resolves via sys.path to a location not among the candidates (pipeline_dir, cwd), edits to the real module won't change the fingerprint -> stale preview/trace served. The AST detection also only catches literal `import utility` forms, not aliased/dynamic re-exports.

candidate_risks.concern: FingerprintCache.update_slot, when max_bytes is set and the slot is NOT size-sensitive, preserves the stored byte estimate and bypasses put()/re-measure (move_to_end + direct assignment), trusting the caller's size_sensitive_slots declaration.
candidate_risks.why: If a slot is mis-declared as non-size-sensitive but actually holds a large mutable object that grows, _current_bytes drifts from reality and the byte cap silently stops bounding memory. Correctness hinges on the size_sensitive_slots contract being exhaustive.

candidate_risks.concern: _read_v2_config (route) and _normalise_loaded_config (parser) both strip _API_INPUT_LEGACY_KEYS_TO_STRIP and must agree; the strip set is duplicated by import but the two funnels run different validation (route does is_v2_shape only; parser does full normalise). load_node_config rejects duplicate JSON keys but _read_v2_config (orjson) does NOT reject duplicate keys.
candidate_risks.why: orjson silently keeps the last duplicate key, while json (object_pairs_hook) raises — so the same on-disk config could be accepted differently by the cache-build path vs the parser load path, a divergence the comment explicitly says must not happen.

candidate_risks.concern: build_per_port_cache removes legacy .build-tmp via shutil.rmtree before creating a unique tmp dir, and _swap_dir_into_place removes a legacy .build-old; these legacy fixed-name paths are shared across concurrent xdist/CLI processes for the SAME cache dir even though the build lock is process-local.
candidate_risks.why: The module docstring states the lock is process-local by design (FastAPI is the only production producer), but tests/CLI running multiple processes against one cache dir could have one process rmtree another's legacy staging dir mid-build. Production-safe given the single-producer assumption; a latent multi-process hazard.

complexity_hotspots.what: DataFrameExecutionCache: parquet-backed LRU with scan refcounts, store-window pins, weakref finalizers, and 5 overridden base-class methods (_is_pinned, _capacity_entry_count, _remove_key, get, scan) plus _release_scan single-unlink logic. internal_dataflow: "INGEST (write): GUI clicks 'Cache as Parquet' -> routes/json_cache.build_json_cache resolves+sandbox-checks data path (resolve_runtime_file_path, enforce_project_root) and selects a v2 config (volatile body, else _read_v2_config from disk -> strips legacy keys). build_per_port_cache acquires the per-dir build lock, runs is_per_port_cache_valid no-op trapdoor, records data_file signature BEFORE reading, _iter_records -> shred_to_buffers (single-pass _walk, ShredSkipStats) -> _buffer_to_frame (strict typed Polars) -> pyarrow writes one zstd parquet per emitting table with per-frame footer schema + meta.json into a unique temp dir -> _swap_dir_into_place atomically replaces working/<hash>/. Success marks _session_consulted_hashes. SAVE: mirror_cache_to_committed copies working/<hash>/ -> committed/<hash>/ (gated on session-consulted + fingerprint/data-signature no-op trapdoor). READ (execute): _builders/_codegen call load_v2_api_source -> is_per_port_cache_valid(working) else committed fallback -> load_per_port_cache scans the parquets -> LazyFrame(s). KEYING: graph._haute_base_fingerprint (sorted node walk -> canonical_json configs + sorted edge-wiring JSON -> content_hash) + preamble_execution_fingerprint (preamble + hashed utility files) + extra_keys -> 'v5:'-prefixed digest -> FingerprintCache slot dict (preview/trace) / dataframe_execution_cache_key payload digest. INVALIDATION: cache_state_signature_for_graph folds each apiInput's working+committed meta.json mtime into the preview/trace fingerprint, and ALGO_VERSION prefix gates algorithm changes. JSON-safety (to_json_safe) is applied only at the API-response boundary, separate from digest material."
concurrency_model: "Several independent lock domains, all process-local. (1) LRUCache uses a single threading.RLock guarding _data/_pinned/_sizes; FingerprintCache exposes it via .lock for caller read-modify-write; all public methods take it. (2) DataFrameExecutionCache adds per-key materialization RLocks (WeakValueDictionary + guard) for same-key write serialization plus a store+first-consume pin window; eviction callbacks (evict_where) deliberately return values so cross-module cleanup runs OUTSIDE the lock to avoid lock-ordering deadlock; unlink deferred to weakref.finalize of consumer scans. (3) _json_shred serializes builds with one threading.Lock per normcased resolved cache dir (_BUILD_LOCKS + guard), publish via atomic dir rename with Windows PermissionError retry. (4) StatGatedCache: global lock + per-key load lock for single-flight, torn-read retry-once-then-raise on a moved (mtime_ns,size) gate. (5) routes/json_cache build-progress dict under its own lock; builds run in FastAPI threadpool. (6) _session_consulted_hashes / _BUILD_LOCKS are unsynchronized-growth module globals (consulted set mutated under no lock — adds only). Notable gap: mirror_cache_to_committed (save path) does NOT take the per-dir build lock while copytree-ing working/ -> committed/, so it is not mutually exclusive with an in-flight build's dir swap."
perf_characteristics: "graph_fingerprint base is O(nodes log nodes + edges log edges) with canonical_json per node config; memoised per PipelineGraph instance via cached_property (hundreds of microseconds for ~100-node graphs, recomputed only on model_copy). preamble_execution_fingerprint re-reads/hashes nearby utility files on every non-empty-preamble call unless a GraphFingerprintMemo is supplied (request-scoped). Shred is single-pass over records, descending only into child keys some emitting table needs (child_keys_by_path prune); parquet write is zstd. is_per_port_cache_valid is stat-fast (size+mtime) and only sha256-hashes the data file on an mtime-only drift. Inference can sample via a hand-rolled streaming JSON-array tokenizer (stops after N object records) to avoid reading whole large files; full builds always parse the whole file. DataFrameExecutionCache spills frames to parquet (bounded by entry count and optional byte budget) rather than holding them in memory; cache hits return scan_parquet LazyFrames. LRU eviction is O(entries) per eviction step (linear scan from LRU end skipping pinned)."
